Supplementary Information The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1186/s44342-026-00081-8. Introduction Nephropathia epidemica (NE) is attributed to Puumala virus (PUUV), a naturally occurring form of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in humans, which is a zoonotic infectious disease and generally considered a mild-to-moderate form of hantavirus infection within the HFRS spectrum. PUUV (Puumala orthohantavirus) is classified within the genus Orthohantavirus, family Hantaviridae, and order Bunyavirales, as defined by current ICTV taxonomy, and it was previously grouped under the family Bunyaviridae prior to taxonomic reclassification. PUUV infection presents with highly variable outcomes, ranging from subclinical cases (70–80%) to severe HFRS, and carries a fatality rate of about 0.1%. PUUV infection commonly presents with sudden fever, headache, back pain, nausea, gastrointestinal symptoms, thrombocytopenia, hematuria, and varying degrees of acute kidney impairment. In some patients, additional manifestations such as blurred vision, dizziness, insomnia, respiratory complications, oliguria, and subsequent polyuria during recovery may also occur. Although PUUV infection is generally considered mild, severe complications can occur in a subset of patients, including acute kidney failure, hypotension, shock, pulmonary edema, Guillain-Barré syndrome, respiratory distress, disseminated intravascular coagulopathy (DIC), myocarditis, encephalitis, pituitary hemorrhage, seizures, and, in rare cases, multiorgan failure or fatal cerebral hemorrhage. The first identification of PUUV occurred in the early 1980s when the virus was isolated from bank voles (Myodes glareolus) in the Puumala region of Finland. Between July 1989 and June 1996, Finland reported 6701 PUUV infection cases confirmed via serological assays, with the highest incidence in the Itä-Savo district and a mortality rate below 0.1%, and later from 1995 to 2008, 22,681 cases were recorded with an average annual incidence of 31 per 100,000 population, resulting in 13 deaths and 52% of patients requiring hospitalization. PUUV accounts for approximately 93% of all notified hantavirus infections in Germany and caused a major outbreak in 2007 in Baden-Württemberg with 1089 reported human cases, while the highest annual number of PUUV infections in Germany was recorded in 2010 since hantavirus surveillance began in 2001. Also in 2007, Sweden’s Västerbotten County experienced a surprisingly severe outbreak of PUUV infection, with NE rates hitting 313 cases per 100,000 residents. Between 2001 and 2017, a total of 12,148 hantavirus disease cases were recorded, of which 9714 (approximately 97.41%) were attributed to PUUV infection. In 2019, Europe recorded over 4000 hantavirus cases (0.8 per 100,000), 98% caused by PUUV, with Finland and Germany making up 69% of the total. From 2018 to 2025, Hungary recorded 51 lab-confirmed hantavirus infections, 20 of which were specifically linked to the PUUV. In Finland, between 560 and 3800 cases of NE are reported each year, though the actual number is believed to be nearly six times higher. PUUV is a spherical enveloped pathogen characterized by a segmented negative-sense single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) genome. The PUUV possesses a tripartite genome: the L segment (~ 6.5 kb) encodes a ~ 2156-amino-acid L protein (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) with replicase, transcriptase, and endonuclease functions; the M segment (~ 3.7 kb) encodes a ~ 1148-amino-acid glycoprotein precursor that is co-translationally cleaved into Gn (70 kDa) and Gc (55 kDa); and the S segment (~ 1.8 kb) encodes a ~ 433-amino-acid nucleocapsid (N) protein. Gc is the protein that mediates fusion by the identification of a peptide of fusion, whereas Gn serves as a folding chaperone for Gc and controls the time of fusion; both are necessary for the virus to adhere as well as enter host cells. Gn and Gc form the principal antigenic surface of PUUV and are major targets of neutralizing antibodies, contributing to protective immunity and vaccine relevance. The N protein plays multiple roles in viral genome transport, replication, and assembly through its interactions with host cellular proteins, while also acting as a highly immunogenic viral component in both humans and animal models. The N protein is highly conserved among orthohantaviruses and elicits a strong early antibody response during acute infection, making it an important target for both diagnostic applications and vaccine development. Various vaccine platforms are available, each possessing distinct advantages and drawbacks. For example, live attenuated vaccines trigger strong, long-lasting immunity but can be risky for immunocompromised individuals due to possible reversion to virulence; inactivated vaccines are safer and more stable, though they usually require multiple doses; subunit vaccines use only key antigens, lowering the chance of side effects, but often need adjuvants and booster shots to achieve durable protection. Moreover, DNA vaccines offer rapid, stable, and cost-effective production with long-lasting immunity, but they often show weak immunogenicity in humans and face delivery challenges. In contrast, the key advantage of mRNA vaccines lies in their rapid design and production, enabling swift responses to emerging infections and pandemic threats without the need to culture live pathogens. In recognition of these advances, the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine honored Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman for their groundbreaking contributions to nucleoside engineering, a key innovation that enabled the successful development of mRNA vaccines against COVID-19. Recent developments in bioinformatics have improved biopharmaceutical design by enabling rapid prediction of protein features, structural modeling, and immunogenicity assessment. These computational approaches accelerate the identification and optimization of therapeutic candidates while reducing time and experimental costs; however, challenges related to prediction accuracy, biological complexity, and the need for experimental validation remain important considerations. Reverse vaccinology (RV) applies bioinformatics and immunoinformatics to screen microbial genomes for conserved, immunogenic epitopes, enabling faster, safer, and cost-effective vaccine development compared to traditional pathogen culturing, a slow and labor-intensive process. Vaccine development against PUUV infection has included inactivated whole-virus vaccines, recombinant subunit vaccines, virus-like particle (VLP)-based approaches, and DNA vaccines. Among these, inactivated and DNA vaccine candidates have demonstrated promising immunogenicity in preclinical studies. Currently, no vaccine has been authorized by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for PUUV infection. Several studies have suggested the potential of multi-epitope vaccine approaches using immunoinformatics-based strategies. Khan et al. developed a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against SARS-CoV-2 by integrating epitope prediction, antigenicity assessment, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and immune response analysis, demonstrating the feasibility of computational vaccine design approaches. Similarly, Peele et al. designed a multi-epitope vaccine construct containing predicted B-cell and T-cell epitopes and evaluated its structural and immunological properties through computational analyses. These studies highlighted the potential of combining multiple immune targets within a single vaccine construct; however, their findings remained primarily dependent on computational predictions and required experimental validation to confirm immunogenicity and protective efficacy. However, despite these advances, several challenges remain in current multi-epitope vaccine development strategies. Computational vaccine designs are dependent on prediction algorithms, reference databases, structural modeling assumptions, and available biological information, which may influence the reliability of predicted vaccine candidates. In addition, variations in epitope selection criteria, antigen conservation analysis, population coverage evaluation, and structural validation approaches can affect the effectiveness of computational vaccine design. Recent studies have emphasized that although immunoinformatics approaches accelerate multi-epitope vaccine development, comprehensive experimental validation remains essential for confirming biological relevance and protective potential. Despite previous vaccine development efforts, including inactivated whole-virus vaccines, recombinant subunit vaccines, virus-like particle (VLP)-based approaches, and DNA vaccine candidates, no PUUV vaccine has currently received regulatory approval. An integrated mRNA multi-epitope vaccine strategy targeting conserved regions of both PUUV glycoproteins (Gn/Gc) and nucleocapsid protein remains insufficiently explored. A comprehensive framework combining conserved antigen identification, multi-epitope vaccine construction, structural evaluation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and immune response prediction for PUUV has not been extensively investigated. Therefore, this study aimed to design and evaluate the PV-GNProtecta vaccine candidate using an integrated immunoinformatics workflow involving conserved antigen identification, epitope prediction, structural modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and immune response prediction. The findings provide computational insights into the potential characteristics of PV-GNProtecta while recognizing the necessity of experimental validation for future assessment. Materials and methods Acquisition and characterization of viral protein sequences The UniProt protein database (https://www.uniprot.org/; accessed on 15 July 2025) was used for obtaining amino acid sequences of the target proteins from PUUV of G (accession number: P41266) and N (accession numbers: P41270). The G and N proteins were selected due to their key roles in PUUV infection and immune recognition. The G protein mediates viral attachment and entry and is a major target of neutralizing antibodies, whereas the highly conserved N protein contributes to viral replication and induces strong immune responses. Compared with the intracellular RdRp/L protein, G and N provide more suitable targets for antibody and cellular immune responses. A comparative evaluation of these proteins is provided in Supplementary Table S14. Physicochemical and structural characterization of selected proteins The selected PUUV G and N proteins were characterized for signal peptide presence, transmembrane regions, and subcellular localization. Signal peptide prediction was performed using SignalP 6.0 (https://services.healthtech.dtu.dk/services/SignalP-6.0/; accessed on 15 September 2026) with the organism group selected as Eukarya and the default prediction model. Transmembrane topology was predicted using DeepTMHMM version 1.0.57 (accessed on 15 September 2026) using the default settings. Subcellular localization information was obtained from UniProt (https://www.uniprot.org/; accessed on 15 September 2026) based on available curated annotations. Analysis of multiple sequence alignment and evolutionary relationships To support RV analysis, the sequence is encoded using amino acid residue codes and preserved as a FASTA sequence file. The acquired sequences were subsequently utilized for multiple sequence alignment (MSA) through the Clustal Omega platform (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/jdispatcher/msa/clustalo; accessed on 05 August 2025). The Mega X tool (https://www.megasoftware.net/; accessed on 05 August 2025) was employed for phylogenetic analysis on both genomes. Prediction of epitopes for MHC I, MHC II, and linear B-cell interactions The MHC I epitopes from the G and N proteins were found using the Immune Epitope Database (IEDB) (http://tools.iedb.org/mhci/; accessed on 20 August 2025) software, with a percentile rank < 1.00 as the selection criterion. This tool is a sophisticated database comprising information on MHC molecules, T-cell and B-cell epitopes, antibodies, and MHC-binding ligands identified in humans and various animal taxonomic groups, including primates and rodents. A cutoff percentile rank of less than 1.00 was implemented for epitope selection, which suggests that the binding affinity was improved. Lower percentile rank values indicate stronger predicted peptide–MHC binding affinity. The IEDB (http://tools.iedb.org/mhcii/; accessed on 20 August 2025) was applied to forecast the MHC II epitopes inside the designated areas of these proteins, and peptides with percentile ranks < 1.00 were considered potential high-affinity binders and selected for further evaluation. Subsequently, the human allele reference sets were employed to predict CD8 + and CD4 + binding. The ABCpred tool (https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/abcpred/; accessed on 25 August 2025) was used to estimate the continuous B-cell epitopes of the selected portions of these proteins. This tool provides epitope predictions by analyzing the sequence features of the target antigens. This program uses an affinity scale method based on a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to predict continuous B-cell epitopes. Additionally, the MHC-II epitopes underwent some additional analyses, including IL-10 (https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/il10pred/; accessed on 25 September 2026), IFN-gamma (https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/ifnepitope/predict.php; accessed on 25 September 2026), IL-2 (https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/il2pred/; accessed on 25 September 2026) and IL-4 (https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/il4pred/design.php; accessed on 25 September 2026) by using the respective servers. Linear B-cell epitopes were forecasted with ABCpred with a standard window length of 16 amino acids and a score cutoff of 0.51. Antigenicity was evaluated using the VaxiJen v2.0 (https://www.ddg-pharmfac.net/vaxijen/VaxiJen/VaxiJen.html; accessed on 28 August 2025) server under the viral protein model with the default threshold value of 0.4. Peptides with antigenicity scores ≥ 0.4 were considered probable antigens and retained for further analysis, whereas those scoring below this threshold were excluded. The threshold value of 0.4 was selected based on the default classification cutoff recommended for the VaxiJen viral model, which was established through performance evaluation of the prediction system. AllerTOP v2.1 (threshold: 0.5) (https://www.ddg-pharmfac.net/allertop_test/; accessed on 28 August 2025) and ToxinPred (threshold: 0.0) servers (https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/toxinpred/algo.php; accessed on 28 August 2025) were deployed in order to make predictions on allergenicity and toxicity, respectively. The allergenicity was evaluated utilizing AllerTOP v2.1 with the server's standard ACC/k-NN algorithm configurations. Also, toxicity prediction was performed using the ToxinPred server with the SVM (Swiss-Prot)-based prediction method, applying the default threshold value of 0.0 and a window length of 17 residues. Peptides were classified according to the server-generated SVM prediction score, and sequences predicted as toxic were excluded, whereas non-toxic peptides were retained for further analysis. All settings were preserved according to the server’s default configuration. The selected epitopes were not chosen based only on prediction scores; additional analyses, including antigenicity, safety assessment, sequence conservation, population coverage, and MHC interaction evaluation, were also considered to improve the reliability of epitope selection. full_text_sections.full_text: Design and in silico evaluation of PV-GNProtecta: an mRNA multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Puumala virus using immunoinformatics and structural analysis Puumala virus (PUUV), the principal causative agent of nephropathia epidemica (NE), poses a significant public health threat due to its zoonotic transmission, renal complications, and the lack of an approved vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-driven mRNA multi-epitope vaccine, PV-GNProtecta, was designed using conserved regions of the viral glycoprotein (G) and nucleoprotein (N). Highly antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic T-cell and B-cell epitopes were identified and assembled with appropriate adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity. Population coverage analysis suggested broad HLA responsiveness across diverse populations. The vaccine construct exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, including stability, solubility, and antigenicity. Structural validation predicted high model quality, with 95.5% of residues located in favored Ramachandran regions and an ERRAT score of 91.4. Molecular docking and MM-GBSA analyses predicted favorable computational interactions between PV-GNProtecta and TLR4, while a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation provided computational insights into the dynamic behavior of the vaccine-TLR4 complex. Codon optimization suggested compatibility of the designed sequence with an Escherichia coli-based expression framework. Immune simulation predicted potential humoral and cellular immune response patterns, including changes in IgG, IFN-γ, and IL-2 levels. The designed mRNA sequence exhibited favorable predicted secondary structural characteristics; however, further experimental evaluation is required to assess translational efficiency and stability. Although this study is limited to computational analyses and requires experimental validation, the findings suggest that PV-GNProtecta may represent a potential candidate for further investigation against PUUV infection. Supplementary Information The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1186/s44342-026-00081-8. Introduction Nephropathia epidemica (NE) is attributed to Puumala virus (PUUV), a naturally occurring form of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in humans, which is a zoonotic infectious disease and generally considered a mild-to-moderate form of hantavirus infection within the HFRS spectrum. PUUV (Puumala orthohantavirus) is classified within the genus Orthohantavirus, family Hantaviridae, and order Bunyavirales, as defined by current ICTV taxonomy, and it was previously grouped under the family Bunyaviridae prior to taxonomic reclassification. PUUV infection presents with highly variable outcomes, ranging from subclinical cases (70–80%) to severe HFRS, and carries a fatality rate of about 0.1%. PUUV infection commonly presents with sudden fever, headache, back pain, nausea, gastrointestinal symptoms, thrombocytopenia, hematuria, and varying degrees of acute kidney impairment. In some patients, additional manifestations such as blurred vision, dizziness, insomnia, respiratory complications, oliguria, and subsequent polyuria during recovery may also occur. Although PUUV infection is generally considered mild, severe complications can occur in a subset of patients, including acute kidney failure, hypotension, shock, pulmonary edema, Guillain-Barré syndrome, respiratory distress, disseminated intravascular coagulopathy (DIC), myocarditis, encephalitis, pituitary hemorrhage, seizures, and, in rare cases, multiorgan failure or fatal cerebral hemorrhage. The first identification of PUUV occurred in the early 1980s when the virus was isolated from bank voles (Myodes glareolus) in the Puumala region of Finland. Between July 1989 and June 1996, Finland reported 6701 PUUV infection cases confirmed via serological assays, with the highest incidence in the Itä-Savo district and a mortality rate below 0.1%, and later from 1995 to 2008, 22,681 cases were recorded with an average annual incidence of 31 per 100,000 population, resulting in 13 deaths and 52% of patients requiring hospitalization. PUUV accounts for approximately 93% of all notified hantavirus infections in Germany and caused a major outbreak in 2007 in Baden-Württemberg with 1089 reported human cases, while the highest annual number of PUUV infections in Germany was recorded in 2010 since hantavirus surveillance began in 2001. Also in 2007, Sweden’s Västerbotten County experienced a surprisingly severe outbreak of PUUV infection, with NE rates hitting 313 cases per 100,000 residents. Between 2001 and 2017, a total of 12,148 hantavirus disease cases were recorded, of which 9714 (approximately 97.41%) were attributed to PUUV infection. In 2019, Europe recorded over 4000 hantavirus cases (0.8 per 100,000), 98% caused by PUUV, with Finland and Germany making up 69% of the total. From 2018 to 2025, Hungary recorded 51 lab-confirmed hantavirus infections, 20 of which were specifically linked to the PUUV. In Finland, between 560 and 3800 cases of NE are reported each year, though the actual number is believed to be nearly six times higher. PUUV is a spherical enveloped pathogen characterized by a segmented negative-sense single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) genome. The PUUV possesses a tripartite genome: the L segment (~ 6.5 kb) encodes a ~ 2156-amino-acid L protein (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) with replicase, transcriptase, and endonuclease functions; the M segment (~ 3.7 kb) encodes a ~ 1148-amino-acid glycoprotein precursor that is co-translationally cleaved into Gn (70 kDa) and Gc (55 kDa); and the S segment (~ 1.8 kb) encodes a ~ 433-amino-acid nucleocapsid (N) protein. Gc is the protein that mediates fusion by the identification of a peptide of fusion, whereas Gn serves as a folding chaperone for Gc and controls the time of fusion; both are necessary for the virus to adhere as well as enter host cells. Gn and Gc form the principal antigenic surface of PUUV and are major targets of neutralizing antibodies, contributing to protective immunity and vaccine relevance. The N protein plays multiple roles in viral genome transport, replication, and assembly through its interactions with host cellular proteins, while also acting as a highly immunogenic viral component in both humans and animal models. The N protein is highly conserved among orthohantaviruses and elicits a strong early antibody response during acute infection, making it an important target for both diagnostic applications and vaccine development. Various vaccine platforms are available, each possessing distinct advantages and drawbacks. For example, live attenuated vaccines trigger strong, long-lasting immunity but can be risky for immunocompromised individuals due to possible reversion to virulence; inactivated vaccines are safer and more stable, though they usually require multiple doses; subunit vaccines use only key antigens, lowering the chance of side effects, but often need adjuvants and booster shots to achieve durable protection. Moreover, DNA vaccines offer rapid, stable, and cost-effective production with long-lasting immunity, but they often show weak immunogenicity in humans and face delivery challenges. In contrast, the key advantage of mRNA vaccines lies in their rapid design and production, enabling swift responses to emerging infections and pandemic threats without the need to culture live pathogens. In recognition of these advances, the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine honored Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman for their groundbreaking contributions to nucleoside engineering, a key innovation that enabled the successful development of mRNA vaccines against COVID-19. Recent developments in bioinformatics have improved biopharmaceutical design by enabling rapid prediction of protein features, structural modeling, and immunogenicity assessment. papers.title: Framing the 2026 Global Hantavirus Outbreak in Nigerian Online Newspapers: Insights from Premium Times and Sahara Reporters
papers.abstract: Background: Emerging infectious diseases often attract significant media attention because of their potential impact on public health perceptions and preparedness. Despite the absence of confirmed cases in Nigeria, the 2026 Andes hantavirus outbreak generated global public health concern because of increased international mobility and the potential risk of cross-border transmission. Objective: This study investigated how Premium Times and Sahara Reporters framed the 2026 global hantavirus outbreak, focusing on the frequency, presentation formats, prominence, and dominant frames of coverage. Method: The study employed a content analysis design. Using census approach, all hantavirus-related stories published by Premium Times and Sahara Reporters between 2 and 30 May 2026 were identified, yielding 29 stories for analysis. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, while Holsti’s (1969) formula was used to assess inter-coder reliability, yielding a reliability coefficient of 0.85. Results: Premium Times published 17 stories (58.6%), while Sahara Reporters published 12 stories (41.4%). Of the 29 stories, 24 (82.8%) were news stories, 19 (65.5%) received low prominence, and 10 (34.5%) adopted a health risk/awareness frame, followed by the prevention and safety measures frame (5 stories; 17.2%) and the attribution of responsibility frame (4 stories; 13.8%). Conclusion: Nigerian online newspapers reported the outbreak primarily as a public health risk but devoted limited attention and prominence to the issue, suggesting a predominantly reactive orientation in the newspapers' reporting of emerging health threats. Unique Contribution: This study contributes empirical evidence on Nigerian media framing of the 2026 global hantavirus outbreak and extends health communication scholarship on emerging zoonotic diseases. Key Recommendation: Nigerian online newspapers should adopt more sustained, prominent, explanatory, and interpretative reporting of emerging infectious diseases to strengthen public preparedness and risk communication.
authors: Valentine Okwudilichukwu Ezema, Sunday Uche Aja, Mercy Ifeyinwa Obichili, Joseph N. Chukwu, Chika Thonia Ezeali, Ijeoma Njideka Taiwo & Kelvin Chinemerem Nkwuda

papers.title: Hantavirus Outbreak on MV Hondius Cruise Ship: India’s Port Health Preparedness – A One Health Perspective
papers.abstract: Abstract The MV Hondius outbreak, reported in May 2026, is among the first large multinational hantavirus clusters linked to cruise ship travel. By July 2, 2026, when the outbreak was declared over, 13 cases (12 laboratory-confirmed and one probable) and three deaths had been reported, with contact tracing involving 33 countries and territories; no confirmed cases were reported in India. The identified Andes virus strain is notable for limited person-to-person transmission. This viewpoint is an interpretation of the outbreak using publicly available reports, scientific literature, and official communications from health agencies within a One Health framework, focusing on implications for India’s port health preparedness. The outbreak highlights how ecological exposure, international mobility, and a confined maritime environment can facilitate disease spread. India’s port health infrastructure includes pre-arrival vessel risk assessment, passenger thermal scanning, and contingency plans aligned with the International Health Regulations (IHR) 2005. Although hantavirus strains identified in India are not associated with person-to-person transmission, existing seroprevalence data support the need for continued surveillance. Strengthening a One Health approach integrating human, animal, and environmental surveillance is essential for future maritime outbreak preparedness. Trained port health personnel, improved diagnostics, and effective public communication remain essential.

analysis.background: The MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak in May‑June 2026, one of the first large multinational cruise‑ship clusters, prompted a review of India’s port health preparedness (A1). The event illustrates how ecological exposure, international mobility, and a confined maritime environment can facilitate disease spread (A6).
analysis.main_directions: The viewpoint uses a One Health framework to examine ecological exposure, mobility, and shipboard transmission, and assesses India’s pre‑arrival vessel risk assessment, thermal scanning, and IHR‑2005 contingency plans (A5, A7). It emphasizes strengthening integrated human‑animal‑environment surveillance for maritime outbreak readiness (A9).
analysis.current_state: By July 2 2026 the outbreak involved 13 cases (12 confirmed) and three deaths, with no confirmed cases in India (A2, A3). The identified Andes virus strain shows limited person‑to‑person transmission (A4), while Indian seroprevalence data indicate hantavirus circulation but no such transmission (A8). Existing port health infrastructure includes risk assessment and thermal scanning (A7).
analysis.gaps: Uncertainty remains about the true transmissibility of the Andes strain in maritime settings and the adequacy of current diagnostics and surveillance to detect low‑level transmission in Indian ports (A4, A8). Improved public communication and training of port health personnel are also needed (A10).
analysis.future_research: Future work should integrate human, animal, and environmental monitoring on ships and at ports, expand diagnostic capacity, train port health staff, and develop clear communication strategies for travelers (A9, A10).

analysis.summary_en: Background: The MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak in May‑June 2026, a large multinational cruise‑ship cluster, highlighted the need to assess India’s port health preparedness (A1, A6). Current state: By July 2 2026 there were 13 cases and three deaths, none in India; the Andes strain shows limited person‑to‑person spread, while Indian seroprevalence indicates hantavirus presence but no transmission, and existing port health measures are in place (A2, A3, A4, A7, A8). Gaps: Uncertainty about transmissibility, diagnostic and surveillance adequacy, and need for better communication and training (A4, A8, A10). Future research: Strengthen human‑animal‑environment monitoring, diagnostic capacity, staff training, and traveler communication within a One Health framework (A9, A10).

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 MV Hondius邮轮疫情:印度港口卫生准备——一体化健康视角

analysis_zh.background: 2026年5月至6月,MV Hondius 汉坦病毒疫情,作为首批大型跨国邮轮集群之一,促使印度港口卫生准备工作进行审查(A1)。该事件说明生态暴露、国际流动和封闭海事环境如何促进疾病传播(A6)。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 该观点采用一体化健康框架,考察生态暴露、流动性和船舶传播,并评估印度入港前船舶风险评估、热扫描及IHR‐2005应急计划(A5,A7)。强调加强人、动物、环境一体化监测,以提升海事疫情应急准备(A9)。
analysis_zh.current_state: 截至2026年7月2日,疫情共涉及13例(12例确诊)和3例死亡,印度未出现确诊病例(A2,A3)。已鉴定的安第斯病毒株显示人际传播有限(A4),而印度血清流行率数据显示汉坦病毒流通但无此类传播(A8)。现有港口卫生基础设施包括风险评估和热扫描(A7)。

papers.title: Rising spillover risk: Lessons from the Andes hantavirus outbreak
papers.abstract: The unprecedented expansion of human activity boundaries is turning spillover from a chance event into a foreseeable ecological and epidemiological certainty. Using the 2026 Andes hantavirus cruise ship outbreak as an entry point, this study examines it within a broader driver framework: nearly all emerging infectious disease events in humans in recent decades have originated from wildlife transmission; under climate-change and land-use scenarios, approximately 3139 mammal species are projected to aggregate in new combinations by 2070, causing an estimated 4000 cross-species viral transmission events. The rapid expansion of tourism into ecologically fragile regions — sub-Antarctic waters, the deep sea, and primary forests — the persistence of habitat fragmentation and animal trade, and the reshaping of wildlife distribution and vector dynamics by extreme climate events together constitute “novel contact amplifiers” that accelerate contact at the human–animal–environment interface. Robotics, artificial intelligence, autonomous driving, and automated logistics are extending human activities into previously inaccessible regions, yet they remain almost entirely absent from current spillover risk assessments. The limitations of cruise ship medical systems — whose core capacity lies in “recognize, isolate, stabilize, and transfer” rather than definitive diagnosis and treatment — were fully exposed in this event. From a One Health perspective, this paper proposes that responses to spillover risk must shift from passive reaction to proactive interface governance, incorporate technology-driven increases in contact frequency into prevention and control frameworks, and advance cornerstone strategies such as broad-spectrum vaccines and broad-spectrum antiviral drugs at the basic research level.

papers.title_zh: 上升的溢出风险:安第斯病毒 汉坦病毒 疫情的经验教训

analysis_zh.background: 人类活动边界的扩张正在将跨种传播变为可预见的必然;2026年安第斯病毒汉坦病毒号邮轮疫情被用作检视驱动因素的切入点。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究以2026年安第斯病毒汉坦病毒号邮轮疫情为案例,置于更广泛的驱动因素框架内;具体设计细节未在所提供证据中报告。
analysis_zh.results: 气候变化与土地利用情景预测到2070年将有3,139种哺乳动物在新的组合中聚集,可能导致约4,000起跨种病毒传播事件;快速的旅游扩张、栖息地碎片化、动物贸易和极端气候事件充当新的接触放大器。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本文主张在基础研究层面实施主动界面治理、技术驱动的预防,以及研发广谱疫苗和抗病毒药物。
analysis_zh.limitations: 当前跨种传播风险评估忽略了机器人、人工智能、自动驾驶和自动化物流;邮轮医疗系统缺乏明确的诊断和治疗能力。

papers.title: Human febrile illness associated with Yanggou tick virus: Clinical characteristics and epidemiological links to rodents.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: We identified Yanggou tick virus (YGTV), a segmented flavivirus previously unrecognized as a human pathogen, in a patient presenting with fever and headache. This study aims to characterize the epidemiology and clinical manifestations of YGTV infection in patients with fever of unknown origin (FUO). METHODS: We conducted a surveillance study at the First Hospital of Jilin University (2020-2025) involving 1,011 patients with FUO. Concurrently, ticks and rodents in the vicinity of the patients' residences and workplaces were collected for viral detection. YGTV infection was confirmed via PCR assays. Positive samples were used for viral isolation, genome amplification, and phylogenetic characterization. An Apodemus agrarius challenge model was established to evaluate viral persistence and shedding. RESULTS: Of the 30 confirmed cases of YGTV infection, 10 were co-diagnosed with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). The patients showed no clear seasonality or geographic bias. Notably, rodent contact (43.3%) was a more frequent risk factor than tick bites (6.7%). While clinical presentations were non-specific, nearly 50% of the patients presented with gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms. YGTV was isolated from patients, ticks, and A. agrarius (the latter often co-infected with Hantaan virus). Animal models confirmed persistent splenic infection and viral shedding via oral and fecal routes. CONCLUSION: Our findings establish YGTV as an underdiagnosed cause of human febrile illness, underscoring the transmission risks posed by tick vectors and rodent reservoirs. These results highlight the urgent need for enhanced clinical surveillance and diagnostic screening among patients presenting with FUO, particularly in regions where the virus is endemic.

papers.title_zh: 与羊沟蜱病毒相关的人类发热疾病:临床特征及与啮齿动物的流行病学关联

analysis_zh.background: 本研究确认扬沟蜱病毒(YGTV),一种分段黄病毒,作为先前未被识别的人类病原体,导致发热和头痛,并旨在阐明其在发热不明原因(FUO)患者中的流行病学和临床表现。
analysis_zh.methods: 在吉林大学第一医院(2020‐2025)进行的监测研究纳入了1,011名FUO患者;采集并通过PCR检测患者居住/工作地点附近的蜱和啮齿动物,阳性样本用于病毒分离、基因组扩增、系统发育分析,以及使用Apodemus agrarius挑战模型评估病毒持续感染和排泄。
analysis_zh.results: 在30例确诊的YGTV病例中,10例同时诊断为肾综合征出血热;无明显季节性或地域偏向;与蜱叮咬(6.7%)相比,啮齿动物接触(43.3%)是更常见的风险因素;近50%出现胃肠和神经系统症状;YGTV在患者、蜱和A. agrarius中分离,常与汉滩病毒共感染;动物模型显示脾脏持续感染及口腔/粪便排泄。
analysis_zh.contribution: 研究结果确立了YGTV作为人类发热性疾病的被低估病因,强调蜱媒介和啮齿动物宿主的传播风险,并强调在流行地区加强FUO患者的临床监测和诊断筛查的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations: 未在提供的证据中报告。

papers.title: Hantavirus in Dentistry: Occupational Exposure Considerations and a Proposed Tiered Infection Prevention and Control Framework-A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Objective The aim of this study is to synthesize evidence on hantavirus transmission and occupational exposure pathways relevant to dentistry, and to propose an evidence-informed tiered infection prevention and control (IPC) framework that distinguishes established from theoretical risk. Material and methods The initial narrative search covered database inception through May 15, 2026 in MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, and WHO/CDC/ECDC/OSHA sources, followed by a targeted PubMed/MEDLINE and public-health guidance update through August 18, 2026. Approximately 1450 records were identified. After duplicate removal, 1070 records were subjected to title/abstract screening, 215 full-text records were assessed for eligibility, and 45 sources were included in the final synthesis, comprising 34 peer-reviewed publications and 11 gray-literature or public-health guidance sources. Results Environmental exposure to infected-rodent contamination is the established occupational pathway. Limited person-to-person transmission is documented for the Andes virus (ANDV), but no dental transmission has been reported. ANDV RNA and culture-based infectivity have been demonstrated in some oral/respiratory fluids; however, dental-aerosol transmission has not been shown. Dental-specific occupational risk therefore remains unquantified. Conclusions No dental transmission has been documented, and patient-related risk remains uncertain. Standard precautions and rodent control are foundational; suspected or confirmed ANDV warrants transmission-based precautions and airborne precautions for aerosol-generating procedures according to current guidance. The proposed dental tiers are evidence-informed, author-derived, and unvalidated.

papers.title: DNA and mRNA Vaccines Against Hantaviruses: Antigen Design, Delivery Strategies and Translational Progress.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are members of the Hantaviridae family, which can cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). At present, no specific antiviral treatment is available for hantavirus infection, while licensed hantavirus vaccines are restricted to a limited number of countries in Asia. This review summarizes recent advances in hantavirus deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines, focusing on antigen design, delivery systems, immunogenicity, safety and translational development. Peer-reviewed studies published primarily within the past 10 years were evaluated together with available hantavirus vaccine trials registered in ClinicalTrials.gov, with emphasis on Hantaan virus (HTNV), Puumala virus (PUUV) and Andes virus (ANDV). DNA vaccine candidates have demonstrated immunogenicity in preclinical and early clinical studies, with an acceptable safety profile. mRNA vaccines represent a newer approach with promising preclinical evidence of humoral and cellular immune responses. However, they have not yet been evaluated clinically. Studies have also reported the potential for varying degrees of cross-protection between hantavirus species, although protection remains limited by antigenic diversity. Overall, current evidence supports further development of nucleic acid-based hantavirus vaccines, particularly multivalent strategies, with emphasis on standardized evaluation and clinical efficacy.

papers.title: Epidemiology and Economic Burden of Puumala Virus Infection in Styria, Austria, 2003 to 2024.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hantavirus infections cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and impose a potential burden on healthcare systems. However, comprehensive economic data remain scarce. We quantified the inpatient economic burden of hospitalized patients with Puumala virus (PUUV) infections in Styria, Austria's primary endemic region, to identify hospitalization costs and early admission predictors of costs. METHODS: This retrospective cost-of-illness study analyzed 1049 serologically confirmed PUUV hospitalizations across 20 public hospitals in Styria, Austria between September 2003 and March 2024. Costs were estimated using the Austrian performance-oriented hospital financing (Leistungsorientierte Krankenanstaltenfinanzierung) diagnosis-related group system, standardized to 2024-equivalent Euros using consumer price index deflation. Admission predictors of cost were assessed using multivariable γ-generalized linear modeling with multiple imputations. Temporal trends in length of stay were analyzed using weighted segmented linear regression. RESULTS: Cumulative inpatient cost was ∼€10.3 million (mean per-case: €9788) for the entire study period of 21 years. Three epidemic years (2012, 2019, and 2021) accounted for 53.6% of cases and over €5.2 million in expenditure, with peak annual costs reaching €1.93 million (0.274% of total Styrian inpatient expenditure) in 2012. Prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT; cost-ratio 1.024 per second, 95% CI 1.019-1.030) and older age (CR 1.004 per year, 95% CI 1.001-1.008) were independent admission-level predictors of higher cost. Median hospital length of stay declined by ∼50% over the study period. CONCLUSIONS: PUUV hospitalizations impose a sharply episodic but recurrent economic burden on regional healthcare systems. Admission aPTT and age independently predicted cost, but clinical outcomes were not modeled and these variables do not constitute a triage tool. Epidemic preparedness strategies are warranted.

Methods: A retrospective cost‑of‑illness study of 1049 serologically confirmed Puumala virus hospitalizations in 20 public hospitals in Styria, Austria (2003–2024) used the Austrian diagnosis‑related group system, standardized to 2024‑equivalent Euros, with multivariable γ‑GLM and weighted segmented regression to assess cost predictors and length‑of‑stay trends. papers.title_zh: 2003至2024年奥地利施蒂利亚地区 普马拉病毒 感染的流行病学与经济负担。

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒感染导致肾综合征出血热,并对医疗系统造成潜在负担,但全面的经济数据仍然稀缺。
analysis_zh.methods: 回顾性疾病成本研究,涉及1049例在奥地利施蒂利亚州20家公立医院中血清学确诊的普马拉病毒住院病例(2003–2024),采用奥地利诊断相关分组系统,并标准化为2024年等值欧元;入院预测因子通过多变量γ-GLM和多重插补评估,住院时长的时间趋势则用加权分段线性回归分析。
analysis_zh.contribution: PUUV住院病例对地区医疗系统造成明显的间歇性但反复出现的经济负担;入院时的aPTT和年龄独立预测费用,但这些变量并非分诊工具;需要制定疫情防备策略。
analysis_zh.limitations: 未对临床结局进行建模,因此入院时的aPTT和年龄并非分诊工具,且分析仅限于摘要数据。
